rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 1 (score 356.6) was the best design. It finished 18 of 20 oval trials at a mean time of 1.89 s, but it left the line on every s-bend and slalom trial with max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m. The off-track limit for body_width 0.18 is about 0.0575 m. Iteration 2 (score 270.4) changed four things at once: sensor span widened to +/-0.06 m, sensor_size raised to 0.016 m, kp raised to 3.0, and kd raised to 1.0. Its oval finish rate fell from 0.90 to 0.55, control_effort rose from 6.6 to 9.3, and steering_oscillation rose from 0.23 to 0.27. The s-bend and slalom still failed, so the wider span did not fix the bends. The larger sensor footprint and higher kp most likely hurt the oval. I cannot separate the effects from these results alone.

Decision. I return to the iteration 1 controller (kp 2.5, kd 0.8, ki 0.02) and sensor_size 0.012. I change only two things. (1) Widen the sensor span to x = -0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06 m, keeping 5 sensors and the same weights. With 0.012 m footprints and 0.03 m spacing, a 25 mm tape always covers at least one sensor. This tests the span effect alone, since iteration 2 confounded it. (2) Lower base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1. The s-bend and slalom failures are overshoot off the line at higher speed, and the oval margin (1.89 s at 1.3) is enough that a roughly 15 percent speed cut should still finish well under 3 s.

Expected result. Oval completion should hold at about 0.9, with a finish time of roughly 2.1 to 2.3 s. On the s-bend and slalom, max_error should fall below about 0.05 m and progress should rise above 0.5, because the slower speed gives more time to correct and the wider span keeps a signal through the bend.

Hypotheses and next measurements. (a) Most of the bend failures come from speed, so s-bend max_error should drop with base_speed 1.1 even without the span change. (b) If the oval finish time exceeds 2.5 s, the speed cut is too large and the next step is base_speed 1.2. (c) If the s-bend still goes off track with line_loss_events near 1, the sensor span is not the limit and kd should rise to about 1.0 to damp the swing. Please report per-track completion, progress, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and completion_time.
